summary.intent: Get Callisto 0.13.0 released (stacking registry `kind` and moon pin PRs), diagnose why no 0.13 version appeared, verify everything is healthy, and then move back to the latest moon version if it works.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed the failed release as moon 2.6.3 being advertised without downloadable archives, merged #312/#313/#314, re-ran a transient Identify failure to create release PR #316, and opened a moon bump PR for 2.6.3. 0.13.0 is still unpublished pending the user's go-ahead on the recovery dispatch.

repo: The built-in crates.io registry is keyed `cratesIo`, not `crates-io` as docs/config.md said. A `[registries.cratesIo]` entry with only timeouts was read as npm and failed with 'configured for ecosystem npm, not cargo'.
Custom registries now require `kind`; omitting it fails with E321. Built-in `cratesIo`, `npm` and `pypi` keep their own kind.
Release PRs created by the workflow's token do not trigger CI, so they need a manual re-trigger before merge.

The release workflow runs the orchestration at the release commit, so fixes such as the `.prototools` pin only protect runs whose commit includes them. A plain 're-run failed jobs' reuses the old commit and old pin.
Recovery path: `gh workflow run callisto-release.yml -f release_source_sha=<sha>` uses current orchestration with an explicit release commit and adopts anything already landed.

Merging a release PR bumps manifest versions even if publish fails, so main can show 0.13.0 while crates.io is still at 0.12.0. Merging the next release PR (#316, 0.14.0) before recovering would skip 0.13.0.
The 'Identify a merged Callisto release PR' job calls `gh api` with no retry and failed once with `unexpected end of JSON input`.
`.prototools` previously floated moon at `2`, which resolved to 2.6.3 even though only 2.6.2 had release assets.
workflow: When a tool version is advertised but its assets 404, pin to the last good version and verify with CI before floating again.
Check the upstream release assets directly (HTTP status on archives) rather than trusting the version list.
Pre-commit hooks needed moon installed locally, so `proto install` of the pinned version was required.
Actions that publish crates and create releases were not run without user approval; the assistant asked first.

friction: moon 2.6.3 was advertised to proto but its Linux archives returned 404, breaking the aarch64 Linux build in the Release run (39731671178).
Plain re-run could not pick up the moon pin because it reuses the release commit's orchestration.
The Release run on the #314 push failed with a transient `unexpected end of JSON input` in the Identify job, which has no retry.
The user was surprised that no 0.13 version appeared after merging, and the release PR had no CI checks because of the token limitation.
Main is left in an inconsistent state: manifests say 0.13.0 but nothing was published.
